# Codex PPT Slide Image Prompt

## Canvas
{

## Deck Goal
Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers to understand the local development system, route a change to the correct WKND module, and distinguish build validation from installation and runtime verification.

## Required Background
{
  "deck_context": {
    "source_summary": "Class 2 of an eight-week AEM Sites training course. The audience is learning traditional AEM Sites on AEM as a Cloud Service through the WKND project. This class focuses on the local SDK, Maven reactor and repository module responsibilities.",
    "core_claim": "Before editing a file, name the change, identify the module that owns its lifecycle, then verify the assembled result.",
    "canonical_terms": [
      "WKND source project",
      "AEM SDK",
      "Dispatcher Tools",
      "Maven reactor",
      "core",
      "ui.apps",
      "ui.content",
      "ui.config",
      "dispatcher",
      "all",
      "Local Author"
    ]
  },
  "slide_local_context": {
    "required_background": "The generic validation command is mvn clean verify. Installation uses the repository-approved profile, whose exact name must come from the README. After installation, a runtime check is still required."
  }
}

## Global Style
{
  "name": "Detailed AEM repository atlas",
  "visual_direction": "Information-rich technical blueprint blended with professional academic courseware. Each slide should feel specific to AEM and WKND, with credible repository paths, build artifacts, precise annotations and meaningful connectors instead of generic corporate cards.",
  "color_palette": "Warm off-white drafting-paper background; deep navy typography; faint square grid; semantic blue for Java/application code, violet for AEM presentation code, green for configuration, orange for Dispatcher/delivery and slate for package aggregation.",
  "typography": "Crisp modern sans serif headings and labels; true monospace appearance for module names, commands, paths and artifacts; strong hierarchy readable on a projected slide.",
  "texture_and_finish": "Flat 2D technical drawing with fine rules, restrained colored headers, precise folder/file glyphs and subtle drafting-grid texture. No gradients, neon, glass, 3D icons or photography.",
  "deck_consistency": "Match the approved sample's palette, typography, annotation density, line weight, grid texture and AEM-specific technical precision while varying composition by slide role."
}

## Input Images

- Image 1: /Users/juanmaldonado/Projects/aem-training/slides/lesson-02/origin_image/slide_07.png — approved sample slide style reference; Match style, palette, typography, density and technical precision only; do not copy the exact repository-map layout.


## Slide
{
  "number": 6,
  "title": "Verify first. Install second.",
  "role": "process",
  "intent": "Separate build evidence, installation evidence and functional runtime evidence."
}

## Text
{
  "title": "Verify first. Install second.",
  "key_points": [
    "mvn clean verify — compile, test, package",
    "approved install profile — deploy to Local Author",
    "BUILD SUCCESS ≠ correct page behavior",
    "repository README overrides generic commands"
  ],
  "speaker_focus": "Use the three evidence gates to stop learners from treating BUILD SUCCESS as proof that the feature works."
}

## Layout
{
  "composition": "Detailed three-gate pipeline on a drafting board: VERIFY, INSTALL and RUNTIME CHECK. Under VERIFY show compile/test/package evidence; under INSTALL show package manager and Local Author; under RUNTIME CHECK show the actual WKND page and browser request. Include exact eyebrow '06 · THREE EVIDENCE GATES'.",
  "content_zones": "Title top; pipeline center; command and evidence rows below each gate; README authority note at bottom.",
  "relationship_to_previous_slide": "Turn the module map into an executable validation sequence.",
  "spacing": "Strong left-to-right flow with enough annotation to distinguish artifacts from outcomes."
}

## Visual Elements
{
  "main_visual": "Terminal command enters verify gate, an all package enters install gate, and a Guide page plus response check completes runtime evidence.",
  "supporting_elements": "Evidence tags 'tests pass', 'package installed', 'behavior observed'; an inequality symbol between BUILD SUCCESS and functional proof."
}

## Constraints
[
  "Render the eyebrow exactly as '06 · THREE EVIDENCE GATES'.",
  "Render 'mvn clean verify' and 'BUILD SUCCESS ≠ correct page behavior' exactly.",
  "Do not invent an install profile name."
]

## Style Reference Rule
Use Image 1 as the approved sample-slide style reference. Match its palette, typography mood, density, texture, and overall visual identity. Do not copy its exact layout unless this slide's layout explicitly asks for it.

## Input Image Handling Rules
For any input image marked as a strict input asset, include it visibly and preserve its content. Do not redraw, replace, relabel, or invent a similar figure. Scale and crop only as needed for composition while keeping the important labels, arrows, data, and relationships recognizable.

## Universal Constraints
- The final image itself must contain the title and key points.
- Render Chinese text exactly and legibly; avoid garbled characters.
- Keep the confirmed deck style consistent while varying layout by slide role.
- No watermark, unrelated logo, or extra slide number.
